patients.label: Case 1: 57-year-old male with prior aortic valve replacement, cardiac arrest and cardiogenic shock from bioprosthetic valve stenosis and thrombosis
attribution_limitations: Source conflict on the interval from VA-ECMO start to the redo aortic valve replacement: the case text ("After 3 days") and abstract ("Three days later") print 3 days, Table 3 prints 2 pre-operative ECMO days. Only this interval is quarantined (review_only facts); the year-less summary dates 17 and 19 September give a further arithmetic-only difference.

Source conflict on total ECMO duration: the case description prints a total of 18 days, the discussion prints up to 19 days (12 VA and 7 VV); both are quarantined. Table 3 (12 AV plus 7 VV) differs from 18 only by arithmetic, and the year-less summary dates (17 to 28 September for VA-ECMO) differ from 12 days only by arithmetic.

The summary figure describes cardiogenic shock due to acute myocardial infarction with ST elevation, while the narrative reports coronary angiography without significant lesions and valvular thrombosis as the prosthesis problem. These are different attributes (a stated cause and an angiographic result), so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 1 prints haemoglobin in mg/dL and a lactate reference range printed as 05-1.6 mmol/L; Case 1 left ventricular ejection fraction before surgery is printed as a range 30-35 (percent).

The discussion describes a rigid-wire false path with massive bleeding in obese patients and says the first case was morbidly obese, but the sentence about the false path does not itself name the case.
Escherichia coli coinfection is stated for one of the two cases with K. pneumoniae isolation, without saying which.

The text cites Figure 1D after the redo aortic valve replacement, whereas the Figure 1 caption describes panel D as a dysfunctional bioprosthetic aortic valve; panel C (bilateral alveolar opacities) is not cited in the text.
The case text calls the study cited as Figure 1A and B a transthoracic echocardiography, while the Figure 1 caption describes panels A and B as transoesophageal echocardiograms.
The Figure 1A caption prints the peak velocity as 4.8 ms (a velocity with a time unit); the value is kept as printed. The image measurement box prints its own values, which are pixel content only.
Heart arrest is listed in both the 16 September and 17 September summary rows; the source does not say whether these are the same or two arrests.

patients.label: Case 2: 39-year-old man with two prior mitral valve replacements and cardiogenic shock from prosthetic ring dehiscence
attribution_limitations: Source conflict on regurgitation severity for the same transoesophageal study (the text cites Figure 2A and B): the text says severe mitral regurgitation, the Figure 2A caption says moderate paravalvular leak, both due to ring detachment or dehiscence. Only severity is quarantined; the dehiscence finding stays scored.

ECMO and stay intervals differ only by arithmetic or anchor: the text gives de-cannulation "After 4 days" (anchor not named) and discharge after 11 days; the abstract says weaning 3 days after surgery; Table 3 gives 4 total and 3 post-operative AV days with 0 pre-operative days and an 11-day ICU stay; the year-less summary dates are 20 to 23 March for ECMO and 19 March to 21 April for admission to discharge.
Table 1 labels the single Case #2 column Before ECMO; VA-ECMO was started only after the third redo MVR, so the column does not say whether these values were drawn before or after surgery.
Figure 2C lists right pleural effusion or thickening; the alternative asserts neither.

attribution_limitations: Source conflict on the interval from VA-ECMO start to the redo MVR: the case text ("After 3 days of support") and Table 3 (3 pre-operative days) print 3 days, the abstract prints one day later; all sides are quarantined. The text cites Figure 2B for the Case 3 transthoracic echocardiogram, but Figure 2 is the Case 2 figure and the Case 3 caption places the transthoracic echocardiogram in Figure 3B.

Escherichia coli coinfection is stated for one of the two cases with K. pneumoniae isolation, without saying which.
